title: Cancel-During-Start Relaunch Recovery Matrix
problem: A durable cancellationRequested record can have jobID=null when the app terminates while provider start is in flight. The remote start may have succeeded, so generic missing-binding handling or blind retry is unsafe.

cases.condition: cancellationRequested + jobID=null after relaunch and no stable resolver is available
cases.expected: ambiguousStart; do not delegate to generic missing-binding recovery; do not start a duplicate job

cases.condition: starting/startAmbiguous remains unresolved after stable-idempotent recovery attempt
cases.expected: ambiguousStart; canonical lifecycle is not entered without a durable provider binding

cases.condition: stable-idempotent resolver rebinds the original generation to a provider job
cases.expected: delegate to canonical lifecycle only after resolver has persisted the rebound binding

cases.condition: resolver rebinds a cancellationRequested generation and completes cancellation
cases.expected: preserve cancellation intent; delegate the durable cancelled terminal state to canonical lifecycle

cases.condition: cancellationRequested already has a durable jobID
cases.expected: bypass ambiguous resolver and use normal lifecycle reconnect/cancel observation

cases.condition: UI/startup requests a non-mutating recovery preview for unbound cancellationRequested
cases.expected: ambiguousStart without invoking remote resolver or generic missing-binding path
reuse StableProcessingIdempotencyKey from the same generation; if rebound succeeds, persist binding before remote cancel and cleanup

safety_non_claims: A39 does not prove a live production provider honors idempotency; that remains provider/runtime evidence.
A39 does not prove current-iPhone background termination/relaunch behavior; integrated device evidence remains HQ-owned.
A39 does not promote MOI-P020 from MISSING because the PARITY gate requires integrated long-processing cancellation/retry/interruption evidence.
The formal repository Swift self-test is committed but exact Worker-checkout execution is not observed in this environment.
